description: baseline (LSTM, n_hidden=32, direct_feedthrough, patience-based early stopping)

MODAL_WHITEBOX (2-mode ODE, per-timestep python loop, euler substeps=4): far worse than baseline and computationally infeasible -- only 1-2 epochs completed per fold before hitting the 1800s fold time budget on F16's 70k-117k-sample sequences

MODAL_CONV (2-mode linear modal physics via closed-form free response + FFT causal convolution, no python time loop, nonlinear friction/clearance dropped): computationally viable (full 3000 epochs, no time-budget break) but worse than LSTM baseline -- linear-only physics with 2 modes underfits vs a flexible black-box

GRU (same size as LSTM baseline, only recurrent cell swapped): benchmarked separately -- this PyTorch/CPU build's nn.GRU (and nn.RNN) forward+backward is ~15-27x slower than nn.LSTM for a 50k-step sequence (0.62s vs 16.6s GRU / 9.7s RNN), an infra/backend characteristic not a modeling one -- folds only completed 1-25 epochs before the fold time budget, so this is not a fair architecture comparison; GRU/RNN avoided going forward given this constraint

HYBRID (MODAL_CONV 2-mode physics backbone + LSTM(32) residual on [u,y_phys]): beats LSTM baseline (0.359412 vs 0.418741), new best -- physics backbone gives inductive bias, LSTM residual covers nonlinear friction/clearance + unmodeled modes
HYBRID refinement: backbone n_modes 2->4 (paper's excited band is ~2-15Hz, wider than the 2 named modes): improves val RMSE 0.359412->0.348700, new best
HYBRID refinement: residual_hidden_size 32->64: worse (0.367246 vs 0.348700), early stop at epoch~250 suggests overfitting/instability with larger residual capacity -- revert

TCN: dilated causal conv1d stack (WaveNet-style), channels=32, n_layers=9 (receptive field 1023 samples), y0-conditioned via additive FiLM-style bias per block, no recurrence at all: big improvement over HYBRID (0.248394 vs 0.348700), new best
TCN refinement: channels 32->64: small improvement (0.246480 vs 0.248394), new best

TCN refinement: n_layers 9->11 (receptive field 1023->4095 samples): essentially flat (0.246210 vs 0.246480, noise-level), not a meaningful improvement -- stop refining pure depth/width, try a different modification next
HYBRID_TCN: MODAL_CONV physics backbone (n_modes=4) + TCN residual (channels=64,n_layers=9) on [u,y_phys] instead of LSTM residual: small improvement over pure TCN (0.243444 vs 0.246480), new best

Fixed-iteration ablation: HYBRID_TCN with early_stopping_patience effectively disabled (100000): essentially flat vs run11 (0.244955 vs 0.243444, within noise) -- folds still only reached epoch ~225-375 before the fold time budget (not patience) stopped them, so this model family is genuinely time-budget-limited, not patience-limited; disabling patience doesn't unlock meaningfully more training here

HYBRID_TCN with eval_every 25->50 (less time spent on full-sequence eval bookkeeping, more on gradient steps): essentially flat vs run11 (0.243972 vs 0.243444, within noise) -- extra steps didn't translate into a meaningfully better optimum here
HYBRID_TCN refinement: backbone n_modes 4->6: worse (0.249704 vs 0.243444) -- more physics modes doesn't help once a capable TCN residual is already covering the gap; revert

HYBRID_TCN refinement: residual TCN kernel_size 3->5 (wider per-layer receptive field, receptive field 1023->2047 samples): clear improvement (0.226512 vs 0.243444), new best, biggest gain since run08/run11

HYBRID_TCN refinement: residual kernel_size 5->7: worse (0.231135 vs 0.226512) -- kernel_size=5 was a local optimum, further widening the kernel doesn't help (higher per-layer param count likely trading off against fewer effective steps in the time budget); revert

HYBRID_TCN refinement: channels 64->96 (combined with kernel_size=5): worse (0.250417 vs 0.226512), best_epoch dropped to ~150 -- wider channels overfits/destabilizes faster within the time budget here; revert. Concluding search at 17 completed iterations (>=15-20 floor met) with a stable, repeatedly-refined winner
